newsitem.title: USA: Scudder deal reflects consolidation wave.
newsitem.headline: Scudder deal reflects consolidation wave.

text.p: Zurich Group's planned acquisition of investment management company Scudder, Stevens & Clark reflects continued consolidation in financial services both in the U.S. and globally, analysts said.
The closely-held Scudder, Stevens & Clark, an innovator in some key areas, until recently had a reputation for not aggressively following through on its successes, analysts said.

"In the last year and half new leadership on the mutual fund side of the business has been more aggressive," said Burt Greenwald, a Philadelphia-based mutual fund consultant. Previously, he said, Scudder lost market share when the mutual fund industry began to experience explosive growth beginning about 15 years ago.
Scudder had introduced the first no load mutual fund in the 1920's and in the 1950's the company was a pioneer in making overseas investments via mutual funds.
In a telephone conference call, Scudder chief executive Edmond Villani said the merger positions the company to meet growing demand for investment management services worldwide.

"This combination is driven by strategic considerations on our part and strategic considerations on the part of the Zurich Group," he said. "I give them a lot of credit for farsightedness that they have shown in the discussions, a willingness to have a firm where the employees maintain a significant ownership stake."

Zurich will own 69.5 percent of a new firm to be known as Scudder Kemper Investments Inc in exchange for $867 million in cash and the contribution of Zurich's ownership of Chicago-based Zurich Kemper Investments Inc. Senior employees of Scudder Kemper Investments will own 30.5 percent. The esimtated value of the deal overall is $2.4 billion.

In response to a question, Villani said some of Scudder's retired partners will take mostly cash in the transaction. "Most of us will leave more in the company, significantly more, than we take out," he said.
Zurich Group acquired the Kemper mutual fund business in early 1996.
Analysts noted that Scudder is a direct marketer of its products with no upfront sales load. Kemper relies on distribution of its product through broker channels with a sales charge, or load.
Greenwald said Zurich is getting a "brand name franchise" with a strong presence in the direct market, and thus "covering all the bases" when the business is combined with Kemper.
Villani said the the combination has more elements that are complementary and is not one that is filled with redundancies. The respective products will keep their brand names, he said.

But Villani said a transitional team could be expected to find some redundacies. A Wall Sreet trader said there was immediate speculation that Kemper's Chicago trading operations would be hit hard with activity transferred to Scudder's trading room in New York.
Villani said although separate sales channels will continue, the focus in the combined form will be to move toward one global asset management firm.
He said a key to the future growth of the company is the need to develop retirement systems in most countries of the world.
T. Rowe Price Associates Inc was up 1-3/8 to 49-7/8 in midafternoon in a move traders attributed to speculation about a sale after news of the Scudder deal.
A spokesman said officials of the Baltimore-based investment adviser have stated publicly that their intention is to keep the firm independent.
Asked about speculation that insurance broker Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc might sell its Putnam funds group, a spokesman said the unit is not for sale.

The U.S. has experienced a heavy wave of banking mergers over the last five years and more recently banks have been buying brokers and other firms in an effor to broaden product lines, analysts have said.
